output.name: Taresk
output.myth: Each winter a child who has come through it gets one knot tied in the tail of a kite, and Hesk the Reel keeps the count. Ennu the Kite-Wright made the first for an old woman on the north shore who had come through eighty-one winters. The knots were tight and close. Then Tavo came up the strait laughing, and the spray of the Whale's Blow came with him, climbing into the tail so the knots went heavy. The kite went up full and would not come down. The old woman held the spool with cold hands and did not let go. Aun, who wants to know everything, flew up beside it and asked what the knots were for. Count them, she said, and you will know what you kept. Up in the north-west the Turning Gulls wheeled, watching, and to the east Ennu's black-tailed kite hung where nobody had asked him why. Hesk tied the last knot herself from the far side of the Reel. The kite is still aloft, very high, and every night the children look up and get the knots wrong.
output.finding: Find Mahuri, the Whale's Blow, in the south-west, then look a little less than one hand-span (about 18°) north-east of it for Taresk, the Knot-Count Kite.
